paragraphs.title: The Redemption and the Public Transaction

easy.explanation: Boaz went up to the gate, where the kinsman passed by.
easy.q: Where did Boaz meet the kinsman?

easy.explanation: Boaz took ten men of the elders of the city.
easy.q: How many elders did Boaz gather?

easy.explanation: Boaz first told him that Naomi was selling a parcel of land belonging to Elimelech.
easy.q: What did Boaz first present to the kinsman?

medium.explanation: Boaz presented the matter before the elders so they could witness it.
medium.q: Why did Boaz gather the elders?

answers: He bought the field and then called the kinsman
He met the kinsman, gathered elders, and presented the redemption
He blessed the people and then sought the kinsman
medium.explanation: Boaz first met the kinsman, then gathered the elders, and presented the transaction.
medium.q: What was the order of Boaz’s actions?

medium.explanation: Boaz asked the kinsman to come near and sit with him.
medium.q: What does the phrase “turn aside, sit down here” mean?

answers: It was only a private matter
The transaction had a public and orderly character
challenge.explanation: The elders’ presence made the transaction public and properly witnessed.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Boaz presenting the matter before the elders?

answers: The kinsman had the first right of redemption
The kinsman was one of the city elders
The kinsman had already bought the field
challenge.explanation: Boaz stated that no one could redeem before the kinsman, while Boaz came after him.
challenge.q: Why was it important for Boaz to address the kinsman first?

challenge.explanation: The kinsman explicitly said that he would redeem the land.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the kinsman initially accepted the purchase?

paragraphs.title: Ruth, the Inheritance, and the Sandal Ritual

answers: Ruth and raising up the dead man’s name on his inheritance
easy.explanation: Boaz explained that redeeming the field also involved Ruth and the dead man’s inheritance.
easy.q: What did Boaz add to the offer of redemption?

answers: He feared marring his own inheritance
easy.explanation: The kinsman said he could not redeem it lest he mar his own inheritance.
easy.q: Why did the kinsman refuse to redeem?

easy.explanation: The removal of the shoe was the testimony used to confirm the transaction.
easy.q: What action symbolized the transfer of the transaction to Boaz?

answers: She was included in the redemption so the dead man’s name could be raised up on his inheritance
She sold the inheritance to the kinsman
She was one of the city elders
medium.explanation: Boaz connected buying the field with taking Ruth and raising up the dead man’s name.
medium.q: What was Ruth’s connection to the dead man’s inheritance?

medium.explanation: The kinsman feared that the transaction would damage his own property or family inheritance.
medium.q: What does “mine own inheritance” mean in the kinsman’s statement?

answers: He removed his shoe, Boaz declared the purchase, and the witnesses confirmed it
Boaz blessed Ruth, and the kinsman bought the field
The elders bought the field, and the kinsman changed his mind
medium.explanation: The shoe was removed, Boaz made his public declaration, and the witnesses confirmed it.
medium.q: What happened after the kinsman refused?

answers: It followed a recognized custom in Israel
The kinsman moved into the field
The sandal was a gift to Ruth
challenge.explanation: The passage says this was the former manner in Israel for confirming redemption and exchange.
challenge.q: What does the sandal ritual teach about the transaction?

answers: At first the matter concerned the field alone, but later it included Ruth
At first he refused, but later he agreed
At first Boaz spoke with the people, but later with the elders
challenge.explanation: The kinsman accepted the field at first but withdrew when Ruth and the dead man’s name were included.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the kinsman’s initial agreement and his later refusal?

challenge.explanation: Boaz declared before the elders and people that they were witnesses to his purchase.
challenge.q: Which declaration shows that Boaz completed the transaction?

paragraphs.title: The Blessing of the People and Elders

answers: The people at the gate and the elders
easy.explanation: The people at the gate and the elders said, “We are witnesses.”
easy.q: Who confirmed the transaction and served as witnesses?

easy.explanation: Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife.
easy.q: What did Boaz take Ruth to be?

easy.explanation: The LORD gave Ruth conception, and she bare a son.
easy.q: What did Ruth and Boaz have?

answers: That she would be like Rachel and Leah and build the house of Israel
That she would buy the field
That she would sit at the city gate
medium.explanation: They prayed that Ruth would be like Rachel and Leah, who built the house of Israel.
medium.q: How did the people and elders bless Ruth?

answers: The blessing sought continuation, and Ruth later bore a son
The blessing was given after the son grew up
medium.explanation: The people prayed for fruitfulness and continuation, and Ruth then gave birth to a son.
medium.q: What is the connection between the blessing and the birth of the son?

answers: Succeed and gain an honorable name
medium.explanation: The phrase is a blessing for honorable success and a good name in Ephratah and Bethlehem.
medium.q: What does “do worthily” mean in this blessing?

answers: To connect the new household with family continuity and the building of a family
To say that they were city elders
To explain the price of the field
challenge.explanation: These women were associated with family continuation and the building of Israel’s household.
challenge.q: Why did the people mention Rachel, Leah, and Tamar?

answers: The marriage and transaction received public confirmation
The kinsman remained owner of the field
Only the women knew about the birth
challenge.explanation: Their statement publicly confirmed the transaction and the events connected with it.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the people and elders saying that they were witnesses?

answers: Ruth’s giving birth to a son
challenge.explanation: The blessing for fruitfulness is fulfilled when Ruth bears a son.
challenge.q: Which event fulfills the blessing for fruitfulness?

paragraphs.title: Naomi, the Child, and Family Restoration

easy.explanation: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD.”
easy.q: For whom did the women bless the LORD after the child was born?

easy.explanation: Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became his nurse.
easy.q: Who cared for the child and held him in her bosom?

easy.explanation: The neighboring women called his name Obed.
easy.q: What name did the neighbors give the child?

answers: He would restore her life and nourish her old age
He was one of the elders
medium.explanation: They said that the child would be a restorer of her life and a nourisher of her old age.
medium.q: Why did the women view the child’s birth as restoration for Naomi?

answers: As a daughter-in-law who loved Naomi and was better to her than seven sons
As one of the city elders
As someone who refused to help Naomi
medium.explanation: The women emphasized Ruth’s love and her great value to Naomi.
medium.q: How did the women describe Ruth?

answers: Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David
medium.explanation: The passage says that Obed was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
medium.q: What relationship does the passage establish between Obed and David’s family?

answers: The child became a real part of Naomi’s household and life
Naomi gave the child to the neighbors
Naomi did not know the child
challenge.explanation: Naomi held and cared for the child, showing that he became part of her family life.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Naomi becoming the child’s nurse?

answers: The women viewed Ruth as loving and good, and her son brought comfort to Naomi
Ruth’s love caused the kinsman to refuse
challenge.explanation: The women connected Ruth’s love with the birth of the son who restored and comforted Naomi.
challenge.q: How is Ruth’s love for Naomi connected with family restoration?

answers: The neighbors named the child and connected him with Jesse and David
The kinsman returned to buy the field
challenge.explanation: The neighbors participated, named the child, and identified his place in the family line.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the birth was more than a private event?

easy.q: Who was the father of Obed?
Who was the son of Obed?

easy.explanation: The genealogy ends with Jesse begetting David.
easy.q: Who appears at the end of the genealogy?

medium.explanation: Salmon begat Boaz, Boaz begat Obed, Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
medium.q: What is the correct order of the final generations?
Who was the father of Nahshon?

answers: A list of descendants and family lines
medium.explanation: The word introduces the line of descendants from Pharez to David.
medium.q: What does “generations” mean in the genealogy?

answers: To show the continuing family line from Pharez to David
To explain how the shoe was removed
challenge.explanation: The genealogy connects Pharez’s family line with Obed, Jesse, and David.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the genealogy at the end of the chapter?

answers: Pharez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David
Pharez, Obed, Hezron, David, Ram, Jesse
Pharez, Nahshon, Hezron, Boaz, Amminadab, David
challenge.explanation: This is the complete sequence given in the genealogy.
challenge.q: Which sequence begins with Pharez and ends with David?

answers: Obed’s birth receives a continuing family line leading to Jesse and David
Ruth becomes one of the city elders
challenge.explanation: The chapter moves from Obed’s birth to the generations leading from him to Jesse and David.
challenge.q: What connection does the genealogy make with the events of chapter 4?
